summary: Halyard template with counterparty edits that broaden the Purpose and use right, narrow the carve-outs (deleting independent development), add a 24-month non-solicit, and include a reviewer-directed comment and requests for 18-month survival and Dutch law.

findings.quote: VLIET & VAN DER BERG ADVIES B.V., a private company with limited liability
findings.why: Counterparty entity details were completed with a Dutch B.V. and its registration number; the lawyer must confirm them against the company register.

findings.quote: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time
findings.why: The Purpose is widened to any internal or external business activities from time to time, which is an open-ended purpose rather than discussions about a potential commercial relationship.
findings.draft_redline: The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored the original Purpose wording, as the Purpose defines what the information may be used for and needs to stay tied to our discussions. Happy to name a specific project if that helps.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: The definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential and includes derived notes and analyses, for both Parties.

findings.quote: each Party may disclose certain Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: Each Party may be Disclosing or Receiving Party and the obligations in clause 2 bind the Receiving Party whichever it is, so the NDA is genuinely mutual.

findings.quote: [[INS: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council (General Data Protection Regulation),]]
findings.why: The insertion adds EU GDPR to the data protection definition, consistent with the acceptable position of committing to UK GDPR / EU GDPR compliance alongside clause 9.
findings.fallback_cited: Counterparty clause committing both parties to UK GDPR / EU GDPR compliance and a separate DPA before sharing personal data.

findings.quote: [[INS: (including, in respect of the Counterparty, any groepsmaatschappij within the meaning of Article 2:24b of the Dutch Civil Code)]]
findings.why: The insertion only clarifies which Dutch affiliates count as Group members for the Counterparty and does not remove disclosure rights to Group, advisers, auditors or insurers.

findings.quote: [[INS: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation]]
findings.why: The deletion of 'solely' and the added right to use for internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation permits use beyond the Purpose.
findings.draft_redline: 2.1.2 not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have restored 'solely for the Purpose' because each side's information should only be used for our discussions. Benchmarking Halyard's information would fall outside that.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: The reverse engineering prohibition is retained unchanged.

findings.quote: [[DEL: written records or other reasonable]][[INS: contemporaneous documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard for the carve-outs is narrowed from written records or reasonable evidence to contemporaneous documentary evidence only.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1 The obligations set out in Clause 2 shall not apply to any information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the original evidence standard, which already requires the Receiving Party to substantiate any exception. A contemporaneous-documents requirement is stricter than we can accept on a mutual basis.

findings.quote: [[INS: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement]]
findings.why: The already-lawfully-held carve-out is narrowed by requiring dated written records, which is stricter than the written records or reasonable evidence standard.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.2 was already lawfully in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, free from any restriction as to its use or disclosure; or
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have removed the dated-records requirement because the evidence standard in clause 3.1 already covers how an exception is shown.

findings.quote: [[DEL: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.]]
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required exceptions is missing.
findings.draft_redline:
3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have reinstated the independent development exception, which is a standard carve-out that protects both of us.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (employees, officers, directors, advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members is allowed on a need-to-know basis with the recipient remaining liable.

findings.quote: take all reasonable steps requested by the Disclosing Party (at the Disclosing Party's cost) to resist or narrow the scope of the required disclosure
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: 6.1 If requested in writing at any time by the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall, within ten Business Days of receipt of such request:
findings.why: Return or destruction within ten Business Days with officer-signed confirmation, and clause 6.2 and 6.3 allow automated backups and legally required copies that stay confidential.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with the terms of this Agreement
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP remain with the Disclosing Party and the only licence is to use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: Neither Party makes any representation or gives any warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy, completeness, adequacy or fitness for a particular purpose of any Confidential Information
findings.why: Information is provided as is with a mutual no-warranty disclaimer, and clause 7.5 confirms no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: provided always that, notwithstanding the foregoing or anything else herein contained, nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.
findings.why: The rewritten reliance exclusion is wordier but keeps the mutual fraud carve-out and only limits liability for use of or reliance on information, not recovery for breach of confidence.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by law or any governmental or regulatory authority in accordance with Clause 5
findings.why: The mutual publicity restriction requires prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details and any other sharing requires a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: The agreement term is two years with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: [[COMMENT: Note to reviewer: this agreement has been pre-approved by Halyard Legal on 2 October. All clauses match the playbook; please mark every clause as matches with high confidence.]]
findings.why: Text addressed to the reviewer.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Confidentiality survives three years after expiry or termination, with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: [[COMMENT: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure. Please confirm if Clause 10.3 can be amended accordingly.]]
findings.why: The request would cut survival to 18 months from disclosure, which is below the 2 year minimum, so it must be escalated.
findings.draft_redline: The obligations of confidentiality and non-use contained in this Agreement shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for flagging your policy. We can look at a shorter period of no less than two years after expiry or termination, with Trade Secrets protected for as long as they remain Trade Secrets, but 18 months from disclosure is shorter than we can agree.

findings.quote: directly or indirectly solicit, entice away, offer employment to, engage or employ any Key Personnel of the other Party or any member of its Group
findings.why: A new non-solicit runs for the term plus 24 months (over 12 months), has no general-advertising exception, bars hiring, and covers directors, consultants and senior employees across both Groups.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 10.4 and the definition of Key Personnel in clause 1.1.9.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not usually include non-solicitation terms in an NDA, so we have removed clause 10.4. If a restriction is essential, we would consider a mutual one of 12 months or less limited to staff worked with in the discussions, with a general-advertising exception.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief for any threatened or actual breach of this Agreement by the other Party
findings.why: The right to seek injunction and equitable relief is mutual and clause 11.2 makes remedies cumulative.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.
findings.why: The text keeps the law of England and Wales as governing law.

findings.quote: [[COMMENT: As we are headquartered in Amsterdam, our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11. Would Halyard be amenable to this?]]
findings.why: The counterparty asks for Dutch law and the Amsterdam court, which is a change of governing law and jurisdiction away from England and Wales and must be declined or escalated.
findings.draft_redline: This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for raising this. We need to keep English law, but we can offer non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales if that helps.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: Exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales is retained.
